questions.q: What is the normal temperature of the human body?
questions.why: Normal body temperature is 37 °C (98.6 °F).

questions.q: What is the range of a clinical thermometer?
questions.why: A clinical thermometer is made for body temperature, so it covers 35 °C to 42 °C. The laboratory thermometer covers −10 °C to 110 °C.

questions.q: Why does a clinical thermometer have a kink near the bulb?
options: To stop the mercury falling back on its own
questions.why: The kink holds the mercury in place so the reading stays after you take the thermometer out.

questions.q: What is 100 °C in degrees Fahrenheit?
How does heat from the Sun reach the Earth?
questions.why: Radiation needs no material, and space is empty, so Sun's heat travels by radiation.

questions.q: Which nutrient is called "body-building"?
questions.why: Proteins help the body grow and repair itself.

questions.q: A lack of vitamin C causes which disease?
questions.why: Lack of vitamin C causes scurvy. Rickets is vitamin D, night blindness is vitamin A, and goitre is iodine.

questions.q: What happens when iodine solution is added to a food that has starch?
questions.why: Starch turns iodine blue-black. Violet is the protein test, and an oily patch means fat.

questions.q: Goitre is caused by a lack of ___.
questions.why: Goitre is a swelling in the neck caused by too little iodine. Iodised salt prevents it.

questions.q: Which two nutrients mainly give us energy?
questions.why: Carbohydrates and fats are the energy-giving nutrients.

questions.q: Which method separates husk from grain using the wind?
questions.why: In winnowing, the wind blows away the light husk while the heavy grain falls down.

questions.q: How do we get salt from sea water?
questions.why: The water evaporates in the sun and the salt is left behind.

questions.q: What is the correct order for cleaning muddy water?
questions.why: First let the mud settle (sedimentation), then pour off the top (decantation), then filter the rest.

questions.q: Which method separates iron filings from sand?
questions.why: A magnet pulls out the iron and leaves the sand.

questions.q: Why can't filtration separate salt from salt water?
options: Salt is dissolved and passes through the filter
questions.why: Dissolved salt is in tiny particles that pass through the filter paper along with the water.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of length?
questions.why: The metre is the standard SI unit of length.

questions.q: A car covers 120 km in 2 hours. What is its speed?
questions.why: Speed = distance ÷ time = 120 ÷ 2 = 60 km/h.

questions.q: What type of motion does a ceiling fan show?
questions.why: The blades spin around a fixed centre, which is rotational motion.

questions.q: What is 54 km/h in m/s?
questions.why: Multiply by 5/18: 54 × 5/18 = 15 m/s.

questions.q: A swing moves to and fro. What kind of motion is this?
questions.why: Back-and-forth motion around a middle point is oscillatory.

questions.q: A whale is a ___.
questions.why: A whale breathes air, gives birth, and feeds its young with milk. These are mammal features.

questions.q: How many legs does a spider have?
questions.why: Spiders have 8 legs. Insects have 6.

questions.q: A pea plant has a weak stem and climbs up a support. What group is it?
questions.why: Plants with weak stems that climb on supports are climbers.

questions.q: Which of these is a vertebrate?
questions.why: A frog has a backbone. Ants, spiders and snails don't.

questions.q: How does a cactus survive in the desert?
options: It has thin leaves to catch rain
questions.why: The thick stem stores water, and the leaves are spines, which cut down water loss.
